variants.text: The lines in the glass have ends, and the ends are down there. Reading them would want the lens the cutters will not sell — and going down after them would want something that does not mind heat, going by what comes up.
Air comes up off the stair that dries your mouth in one breath. Whatever is at the bottom of this has a fire under it, and the city has been drinking the runoff for two hundred years without asking.
Masonry under poured glass. Somebody sealed this from above, in a hurry, with the most permanent thing they had to hand.
